text.p: Ecu/drachma pierced the 311 level on ecu buying from abroad, short-term forex forwards were firmer on early funding for coupon bonds to be auctioned on June 19 and bonds fell on profit-taking, traders said.

"The drachma has been losing ground against the ecu since this morning on ecu buying from abroad," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "Ecu/drachma has come off highs of 311.40/50 to trade around 311.28/38 in late trade."
The central bank checked dollar/drachma rates twice after the spot ecu/drachma cross breached 311, the dealer said.

"It is obvious that the central bank is not pleased with the sharp rise of the ecu today," the dealer said. "I was told by London-based traders that this might relate to the speculative attack on the Czech crown and the Thai currency but I do not see the connection."

The Czech and Thai currencies have come under speculative attach lately and analysts said on Wednesday that the success or failure of their authorities to defend them could have repercussions for other currencies around the globe.

Fixed coupon bonds came under pressure with three-year fixed coupon bond prices shedding 30 to 40 basis points and five-and seven-year fixed coupon bonds losing 50 basis points as players rushed to unload them in order to obtain funding for the June 19 auction, dealers said.

"Three-, five-and seven-year bonds have lost ground on profit-taking after the minister's announcement," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "Some banks have decided to take profits as they seek funding for the new paper driving bond prices lower."

Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said the treasury will issue 12-month T-bills at 9.60 percent on June 2, down 10 basis points, and reopen bids for three-, five- and seven-year coupon bonds on June 19.
Greece auctioned three-year, 9.80 percent bonds, five-year, 9.20 percent bonds and seven-year, 8.9 percent bonds on March 19.
The finance ministry will also auction 10-year fixed coupon bonds, the first ever in Greece, on June 19.

Depos were little changed but short-term implied drachma rates were up 20 basis points in tenors up to two-months in late dealings as banks sought early funding for the June 19 auction and T-bill issue on June 2.

"Implied drachma rates from forex forwards have firmed 20 basis points in periods up to two-months and 15 basis points in three-months," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It is definitely linked with early funding for the new bonds and T-bills."
The mark was quoted at 159.40/50 from Thursday's 159.450 fix, the dollar at 269.51/61 drachmas from 269.560 and the ecu at 311.08/18 from 311.080 drachmas.
